newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds again stalled by jobs caution.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds again stalled by jobs caution.

text.p: *Australian bond yields showed only minor movements in early trade with the market looking set for another slow session ahead of the Thursday's key labour force data.
*Market fails to keep pace with firm tone of U.S.
Australian bond yields showed only minor movements in early trade with the market looking set for another slow session ahead of the Thursday's key labour force report for June.

The market had firmed in after hours trading with the 10-year bond futures contract again testing its recent 3-1/2 year peak of 93.210 as U.S. Treasuries retained its strong rally on return from Friday's Independence Day holiday.
The U.S. 30-year bond yield closed at its lowest level since February at 6.58 percent, down four basis points, and just above an intra day low of 6.56 percent.

The U.S. rally was spurred on, albeit in light trade, amid expectations that the Federal Reserve will keep policy on hold in August and on hopes that central bank gold sales will be in favour of U.S. Treasuries.

The recent slump in the gold price, along with other weakening commodity prices, and concerns that the Reserve Bank may ease policy again continues to weigh on the Australian dollar, touching an 18-month low of US$0.7420 in offshore trade.
"Weakness in the dollar could reduce the chances of an easing, but the debt market doesn't seem to be concerned about that at the moment. Nobody wants to be short," one trader said.

The local market's inaction saw it again largely dragging its heels against the dollar bloc. The Canadian market outperformed the U.S. with technical factors helping its 30-year bond yield reach an all-time low. Further weakness in the New Zealand TWI weighed on the short end of the N.Z. curve.
